subject.title: Telegram: allow native channel commands in explicitly allowed chats

question: Should Telegram channel_post native/plugin commands be allowed by explicit chat allow alone, or must sender_chat/per-channel policy and callback session semantics be fixed before this PR can land?
rationale: The PR changes a Telegram command execution boundary and the paired policy issue remains open, so automation should not choose the permanent authorization semantics.

options.title: Fix auth and callbacks first
options.body: Require explicit channel authorization, sender_chat-aware allowlist handling, callback/session routing, tests, and live Telegram proof before merge.

options.title: Pause for policy issue
options.body: Use the paired open policy issue to decide channel_post sender-scoped allowFrom semantics before changing runtime behavior.

options.title: Accept explicit-chat-only semantics
options.body: Maintainers can choose the PR boundary intentionally, but should document the security rationale and require live Telegram proof.

recommendation.title: Fix auth and callbacks first
recommendation.body: Require explicit channel authorization, sender_chat-aware allowlist handling, callback/session routing, tests, and live Telegram proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history ties this owner to Telegram group-access policy and docs surfaces where the authorization decision should be encoded.
